boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Montclair traditions, from Red Hawk rituals and Homecoming activities to a clearly marked historical practice.

cards.title: Throw the Hawk gesture
cards.subtitle: American Sign Language for “hawk”
cards.notes: Use Montclair’s ASL-for-“hawk” hand sign at campus activities and events when you want to show Red Hawk pride.
cards.short_summary: A school-pride hand sign built from the ASL sign for “hawk.”
cards.evidence_claim: Montclair identifies “The Hawk” gesture as a school-pride tradition and says it uses the American Sign Language sign for “hawk.”
cards.access_notes: Use respectfully at University activities and events.

cards.entity_name: Picture with Rocky the Red Hawk
cards.title: Take a photo with Rocky
cards.subtitle: Rocky the Red Hawk mascot
cards.notes: When Rocky appears at Homecoming or another University event, say hello, offer a high-five, and take a commemorative photo.
cards.short_summary: A photo-op tradition with Montclair’s Red Hawk mascot.
cards.evidence_claim: Montclair’s Homecoming pride page encourages attendees to high-five Rocky the Red Hawk and take a picture with him.
cards.access_notes: Rocky’s appearances vary by event; keep an appropriate distance and follow staff direction.

cards.title: Rub the Red Hawk’s beak
cards.subtitle: For good luck during finals and game days
cards.notes: Visit the bronze Red Hawk statue before finals or a game day and rub its beak, the University’s documented good-luck ritual.
cards.short_summary: A luck ritual centered on the campus’s bronze Red Hawk statue.
cards.evidence_claim: Montclair’s admissions magazine says students rub the Red Hawk statue’s beak for good luck during finals and on game days.
cards.access_notes: The ritual concerns the statue’s beak; treat the artwork and surrounding area respectfully.

cards.title: Come back for Homecoming
cards.subtitle: Annual Red Hawk reunion weekend
cards.notes: Join the University’s Homecoming and Family Weekend programming to connect around campus activities, sports, and Red Hawk spirit.
cards.short_summary: Montclair’s recurring fall gathering for students, alumni, families, and the wider campus community.
cards.evidence_claim: Montclair’s 2026 Homecoming schedule describes a weekend of campus events and identifies Saturday as Montclair Campus Homecoming and Family Day.
cards.access_notes: Check the current Homecoming schedule for registration and event-specific details.

cards.title: Make a Homecoming banner
cards.subtitle: A themed campus-spirit contest
cards.notes: If your recognized group participates, design a banner around that year’s Homecoming theme and follow the published contest guidelines.
cards.short_summary: Recognized campus groups demonstrate their Homecoming spirit through themed banners.
cards.evidence_claim: Montclair calls Homecoming an annual campus-wide tradition and documents a Homecoming Banner Contest for clubs, organizations, departments, and residence halls.
cards.access_notes: Participation is for recognized University groups and is governed by the applicable annual rules.

cards.title: See the Homecoming talent showcase
cards.subtitle: Historic Amphitheater performance tradition
cards.notes: Look for the annual student talent showcase during Homecoming and support performers at the historic Amphitheater.
cards.short_summary: A student performance event woven into Montclair’s Homecoming celebration.
cards.evidence_claim: Montclair’s 2022 Homecoming recap identifies the annual student talent showcase at the historic Amphitheater as part of the celebration.
cards.access_notes: Programming and performer registration vary by year; consult current Homecoming information.

cards.title: Mark Red Hawk Day
cards.subtitle: University calendar tradition
cards.notes: Add Red Hawk Day to your fall calendar and use current University announcements to find that year’s campus programming.
cards.short_summary: A named University event that appears on Montclair’s official calendar.
cards.evidence_claim: Montclair’s official Important Dates page lists Red Hawk Day as a University event on August 27, 2026.
cards.access_notes: Date and activities can change; verify the current University calendar before attending.

cards.title: Look for Red Hawk Night
cards.subtitle: Campuswide Student Life tradition
cards.notes: Watch Student Life announcements for Red Hawk Night, a named campuswide tradition included in the division’s annual report.
cards.short_summary: A recurring campus-life tradition supported by Student Development and Campus Life.
cards.evidence_claim: Montclair’s Student Development and Campus Life 2025 impact report lists Red Hawk Night among campuswide traditions it organized and collaborated on.
cards.source_title: Student Development and Campus Life 2025 Impact Report
cards.access_notes: Consult Student Life announcements for the current program, location, and participation details.

cards.title: Spot the yellow talons at Commencement
cards.subtitle: Team Rocky identity reveal
cards.notes: At Commencement, watch for graduating Team Rocky members who reveal their secret mascot identities by wearing Rocky’s yellow talons.
cards.short_summary: Montclair mascots keep their identities secret until their graduation reveal.
cards.evidence_claim: Montclair’s 2025 Commencement story says Team Rocky members keep their identities secret until graduation and traditionally wear Rocky’s yellow talons for the reveal.
cards.source_title: Meet the Students Behind the Mascots: Team Rocky Takes a Bow at Commencement 2025
cards.access_notes: This is an observation tradition at Commencement; mascot identities are to remain private until their reveal.

cards.title: Learn about the discontinued dink-hat custom
cards.subtitle: Historical freshman hazing, ended in the early 1970s
cards.notes: Read the University Libraries archive for context on this discontinued freshman custom; do not reenact its hazing-related practices.
cards.short_summary: A historical Montclair freshman custom preserved as an archival record, not a current activity.
cards.evidence_claim: Montclair University Libraries reports that freshmen once wore “dink” beanies and placards for a week, and that the hazing and dink hats ended in the early 1970s.
cards.access_notes: Discontinued historical practice. Read the archival account only; it is not a current or recommended activity.
